**Written Statement Regarding October 27 Afternoon Route**  
**Bus 41, Route 9 – Fairmont Elementary**

**To:** Mrs. Okafor, parent of Amara Okafor  
**Copy to:** Transportation Office and personnel file  
**From:** [Your Name], School Bus Driver  
**Date:** [Date submitted]  
**Regarding:** Complaint dated October 29, received from Darlene on November 3

Dear Mrs. Okafor:

I am submitting this statement at the request of my supervisor, Darlene, to give my account of what happened on Bus 41 during the afternoon run on Tuesday, October 27. I understand that this statement will be placed in my file and that a copy will be provided to you. I want to be accurate, respectful, and clear about what I saw, what I did, and why I did it.

Before explaining the timeline, I want to say that I understand why you were frightened. You expected Amara to get off the bus at her stop, and when she did not, you had an afternoon no parent wants to have. I have grandchildren, and if one of them did not get off the bus when expected, I would be frightened too until I knew exactly where they were. I am sincerely sorry that you and Amara went through that. Her safety was the reason for every decision I made that afternoon.

Amara is a kindergarten student at Fairmont Elementary and rides Bus 41 on Route 9. She has a green tag on her bag, which indicates that an adult must be present at her stop before she can be released. Her stop is at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street.

On October 27, the scheduled arrival time at that stop was 3:50 p.m. I arrived at approximately 3:52 p.m. I waited until approximately 3:55 p.m., looking for an adult at the corner, but I did not see anyone I could identify as being there to meet Amara. I then kept her on the bus and followed the district’s procedure for kindergarten riders. Under that procedure, when no adult is present at the stop, the student stays on the bus and is returned to school, and the school office contacts the parent.

At 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch then contacted the school. I still had three more stops to complete and 14 children on the bus. I could not park the bus, get off, and go across the road to look for an adult while leaving those children aboard. Remaining with the students and continuing the route safely was my responsibility. After completing the remaining stops, I returned Amara to Fairmont Elementary, arriving at approximately 4:31 p.m. I personally walked her into the building and placed her in the care of Mrs. Petrakis in the office.

During the additional ride, Amara appeared comfortable. She was coloring on her folder and asked whether she could ride more. I told her that we were going on “a little extra trip.” I wanted to keep her calm and avoid making her feel frightened or as though she had done something wrong. I am thankful that she seemed calm, but I understand that this does not take away from the worry you experienced while trying to find out where she was.

Your complaint states that you were parked across Brandt Street by the laundromat and that you waved, but I would not respond to you. I am not saying that you were not there or that you did not wave. What I can state truthfully is that I did not see you. There was a box truck parked on that side, which affected the view from where I was sitting. I did not intentionally ignore you, and I would not deliberately refuse to acknowledge a parent who was waiting for a child. From the driver’s seat, I did not see an adult at the stop or anyone I could clearly identify as waving for Amara.

I also want to respond directly to the statement that I “drove off laughing.” I was not laughing. As I was pulling out, I was telling a fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down. I was addressing student behavior and safety on the bus, not laughing at you, at Amara, or at the situation. I understand that the afternoon was upsetting, but that description of my actions is not accurate.

As for the concern that I “took” Amara, I want the record to reflect exactly where she was and what happened. She remained aboard Bus 41, under my supervision, while I completed the remaining stops. She was then returned to her own school, and I walked her into the office myself. She was not left unattended, dropped off somewhere else, or released to anyone at the corner. Returning her to Fairmont was not a personal decision directed at you or an attempt to keep her away from you. It was the required safety response when I could not see an adult at her stop.

I have been a school bus driver for 28 years and have had no write-ups. I do not mention that to suggest that my experience means I should not be questioned. I mention it because transporting children safely has been my responsibility for a long time, and I take that responsibility seriously. I also had a similar situation years ago on my route involving a different family. No adult was visible at the stop, so I returned that child to school under the same procedure. The family thanked me afterward. I am not comparing that family to you or suggesting that you should feel the same way. I mention it only to explain that this was not something I invented that day or did for personal reasons. It is a safety practice I have followed before.

Because your complaint concerns what was visible at the stop and my conduct as I drove away, I formally request that the Transportation Office promptly pull and preserve all available onboard camera footage, including audio if available, for Bus 41’s Tuesday, October 27 afternoon run. In particular, I ask that the footage include the approach to Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street, the wait at the stop from approximately 3:52 to 3:55 p.m., my radio communication with dispatch at 3:56 p.m., the departure from the stop, and Amara’s return to Fairmont Elementary at approximately 4:31 p.m. I believe the recording will help establish the timeline, the conditions at the stop, my actions, and the fact that Amara remained safely on the bus until I escorted her into the school office. Since recordings may be kept for only a limited time, I ask that this be done as soon as possible so the footage is not overwritten.

I am sorry for the distress and disruption this caused your family. At the same time, I cannot apologize for following the kindergarten-release procedure I am required to follow. If I were faced with the same circumstances again and could not see an adult at Amara’s stop, my responsibility would still be to keep her safely on the bus and return her to school. I believe both things can be true: I regret how difficult that afternoon was for you, and I believe I made the required safety decision based on what I could see.

For future afternoon drop-offs, I respectfully ask that you stand on the bus side of the street at the stop, where I can clearly see you, or step out of your vehicle and come into clear view at the stop area before Amara is released. A wave from inside a vehicle across the street may not be visible from the driver’s seat, especially when other large vehicles are parked nearby. This is not meant as criticism or an attempt to place blame on you. It is a practical step we can take so that I can confirm an adult is present and prevent this situation from happening again. If the Transportation Office recommends a different arrangement for meeting the bus, I am willing to follow those instructions.

I am glad to continue driving Amara, and I do not want this incident to leave ongoing conflict between us. She will continue to receive the same care and attention as every other child on my bus. I want us to resolve this with clear expectations so that she gets home safely and you can feel confident about what will happen at her stop each day.

Thank you for reading my account and for considering both my responsibility to follow the safety procedure and my sincere wish to avoid another afternoon like this for you and Amara.

Respectfully,

[Your signature]  
[Your printed name]  
School Bus Driver, Bus 41  
Route 9, Fairmont Elementary
